title: Mind maps & dual coding notes
examples: Teacher, how do I make my mind maps look less messy?
Should I use colors in my notes or just black pen?
Is dual coding better than just writing everything down?

explain.say: Today we are learning about mind maps and dual coding notes. These are great ways to remember things better.

items: Dual coding uses words and pictures together.
Both help your brain remember more.

explain.say: First, let us look at branches in mind mapping. Branches show how ideas connect from a main topic.
Next, we will learn about using images with words. Drawing pictures helps your memory work much better.
For example, if you map planets, the Sun is the center. Branches go out to Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars.
Another idea is to draw a picture for 'photosynthesis'. You could draw the sun shining on a leaf.
In real life, think about following cooking instructions. A recipe is like a mind map. The main dish is the center. Branches are steps like 'mix dry ingredients' or 'bake for twenty minutes'.

faq.q: Do I have to use colors for my mind maps?
faq.a: No, you do not have to use colors, but using different colors can help separate your ideas. You might also ask if color is important, or how many colors to use.
asks: Are colors necessary for mind maps?

faq.q: How many branches should I put on one mind map?
faq.a: There is no set number, but try to keep the main branches clear and simple. You could also ask how many main ideas are enough, or if too many branches are bad.
asks: Is there a limit on branches?
Can I put too many ideas on one map?

faq.q: Does dual coding mean I must draw something for every word?
faq.a: No, it means combining words with images when it helps you remember. You might also ask if I need to draw everything, or what counts as an image.
asks: Do I have to draw for every word?
What counts as an image for studying?

faq.q: Is it better to use mind maps or just write notes?
faq.a: Both are good, but mind maps are better for seeing connections between ideas. You could also ask which is better for exams, or if I should use both.

faq.q: Can I use symbols in my mind maps?
faq.a: Yes, using simple symbols like arrows or stars can save space and add visual cues. You might also ask if symbols are okay, or what symbols I can use.
asks: What symbols work well in mind maps?

facts: Mind maps organize information around a central concept.
Dual coding theory suggests combining two sensory inputs boosts memory.
Branches in a mind map show relationships between ideas.
Images help the brain process and recall information more easily.

quiz.say: If the main topic is 'The Water Cycle', which element should be in the center of the map?
quiz.why: The center of the map must always be the main idea you are studying.

wrong.0: A picture is a supporting detail, not the main subject.
wrong.1: Earth is part of the cycle, but not the cycle itself.
wrong.3: This is a detail, not the overall topic.

quiz.say: To remember the parts of a plant, what is the best dual coding technique?

options.show: Labeling a drawing of a plant
options.say: Labeling a drawing of a plant

quiz.why: Labeling combines the word (label) with the visual (drawing), which is dual coding.

wrong.0: This is too much text and loses the quick visual summary.
wrong.2: This only uses words and misses the visual connection.
wrong.3: This only uses pictures and misses the specific names.

quiz.say: When creating a mind map about types of energy, what should the main branches represent?
quiz.why: The main branches must represent the main, separate categories of the topic.

wrong.0: A timeline shows order, not the relationship between types.
wrong.1: A paragraph is dense text and does not show connections well.
wrong.3: A list format is linear, not branching like a mind map.
